subject: Stellarus renewal + reserved pool upsell & SLA amendment
messages:
From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@stellarus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@stellarus.ai>, procurement@stellarus.ai
Date: 2026-10-22T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — Stellarus needs and SLA asks

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the continued partnership. Our renewal is coming up and we want to expand our reserved capacity as part of the new term. High-level ask: increase our committed GPUs from 16 to 56 (40 additional GPUs) across a dedicated US-West pool, with the ability to temporarily burst an extra 8 GPUs for short high-demand campaigns.

Two items we need from Redwood before procurement can sign:
- A written SLA amendment that reflects the expanded pool (throughput guarantees and p95 latency targets for our primary inference profile).
- Explicit credit terms if availability or latency SLOs are missed during or after the migration window.

I attached our internal Q4 forecast for capacity planning. Can we get a rough sketch of latency p95 and expected throughput for the new pool, plus a proposal for the credit schedule? We have a target decision window of two weeks.

Appreciate the quick turn — happy to schedule a call tomorrow afternoon if useful.

Thanks,
Alejandra Ruiz
Head of ML Ops
Stellarus Robotics

Attachments: Stellarus_Forecast_Q4-2026.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: 2026-10-22T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — Stellarus needs and SLA asks

Alejandra — thanks for the clear summary and the forecast.

We're excited about supporting Stellarus' growth. Quick next steps from our side:
- I'll coordinate an internal runbook to size the pool and confirm throughput/latency numbers; looping in Ben (SE) to provide modeling.
- Marissa will lead the commercial/term conversation.
- We can draft an SLA amendment that includes p95 latency targets and a credit schedule; Ben, can you provide simulated p95 numbers for the 56-GPU pool (and a burst scenario +8 GPUs) based on their forecasted QPS?

Can we schedule a 30-minute technical + commercial sync on Monday 10/26? I propose 10:00 AM PT — if that works for you I'll send a calendar invite.

Onward —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Direct: (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — Stellarus needs and SLA asks

Hi Alejandra / Karthik,

I ran a set of simulations against Stellarus' forecast and the proposed 56-GPU dedicated pool. High-level takeaways:
- For your primary inference profile (short prompts, <256 tokens, batch sizes 1–4) we expect p95 latency in the 90–130ms range when the pool is healthy and autoscaling is not throttled.
- Under sustained traffic near the top of the forecast, p95 moves toward ~150–180ms unless automated batching and KV-prefix caching are tuned — we can tune those.
- Burst +8 GPUs (24h reserved burst) reduces p95 by ~20–30% in peak windows for short durations; however there is an onboarding period where KV caches are warm-up sensitive.

Recommendations for the SLA amendment draft:
1) Define workload classes: "interactive-light" (<256 tokens, batch<=4) and "batch-heavy" (>256 tokens or batch>16); apply different p95 targets per class.
2) For dedicated pool baseline (56 GPUs) commit to p95 <= 150ms for interactive-light under normal operating conditions; offer an optional tighter target p95 <= 120ms if Stellarus agrees to a fixed quantized model variant and higher commit.
3) Include a burst window feature: up to 8 GPUs on 24h notice for campaign windows; quality of caching-sensitive workloads should be caveated.
4) Define a graduated credit schedule for latency/availability misses (see attached sim).

I'm attaching the throughput_simulations.xlsx with the curves and charts. Neha, flag anything security/compliance that should be surfaced in the amendment.

—Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: throughput_simulations.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@stellarus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@stellarus.ai>, procurement@stellarus.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T15:18:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — Stellarus needs and SLA asks

Thanks Ben — that level of detail helps. A couple of clarifications from procurement and ops:
1) We will accept a baseline p95 <= 150ms for interactive-light, but we want the SLA amendment to include clear definitions of "normal operating conditions" and an explicit cooldown / warm-up exclusion window for burst usage.
2) For uptime credits: we expect a sliding scale that includes both availability and latency SLOs. For example, if monthly availability drops below 99.9% we request a 20% service credit; if p95 latency breaches the target more than 4 times/month we request an incremental credit.
3) The burst feature is critical — procurement requires the 24-hour notice and that Redwood confirm capacity reservations (we need a signed clause).

I've attached our proposed PO and a short note from procurement on preferred credit thresholds. Can Marissa or legal share a draft amendment that captures the above? Also, procurement would like a 1x onboarding credit to help offset migration/test work.

Best,
Alejandra

Attachments: proposed_po.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@stellarus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — Stellarus needs and SLA asks

Hi Alejandra — appreciate the clarity. Below is a commercial outline we can put into an amendment for legal review: 

Term & capacity
- 18 month renewal (starts on contract execution)
- Reserved pool: 56 GPUs dedicated (US-West) + optional 8 GPU burst for up to 24 hours on request

Pricing
- Standard reserved GPU rate + 12% uplift for the additional committed capacity (we will include per-GPU/month line items in the SOW)
- One-time onboarding credit: 1000 compute hours equivalent (applied as a billing credit)

SLA amendment summary (draft)
- Availability: Monthly uptime target 99.9%; credits: 25% of monthly committed fee for <99.9% and >=99.5%; 50% for <99.5%.
- Latency: Define workload classes; baseline p95 <= 150ms for interactive-light. Optional p95 <= 120ms if Stellarus commits to pinned quantized model variant (price uplift applies). Credits for latency misses will be applied if 1) a monthly aggregated p95 exceeds target AND 2) Redwood verification confirms service-side degradation.
- Burst clause: Redwood will honor up to 8 GPUs on 24h notice; caching/warm-up limitations will be documented and excluded from SLA credit calculations for the first 6 hours after a burst starts.

Next steps
- Attach SLA-Amendment-RD-2026-0432.docx (draft) for review by Stellarus legal and procurement.
- If agreeable, we can route the amendment for e-signature and schedule a short technical run-through to validate caching/warm-up expectations.

Karthik will follow up with a DocuSign packet and next steps. Neha, add any security/retention notes we should include in the amendment.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-Amendment-RD-2026-0432.docx (docx)
From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@stellarus.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@stellarus.ai>, procurement@stellarus.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T09:40:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + reserved pool expansion — Stellarus needs and SLA asks

Marissa / Karthik — thanks for the draft language and the credit schedule. Procurement has reviewed and is broadly aligned. A few final asks before procurement signs:
- Please include the burst clause as written and the 6-hour warm-up exclusion in the amendment text.
- Add the 1x onboarding credit to the statement of work and ensure it appears as a line item credit on the initial invoice.
- Please send the DocuSign packet to procurement@stellarus.ai and copy me; we'll aim to complete legal review this week.

If you can send the DocuSign link today and the final SOW, we can route internally and expedite signatures. Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to closing.

Best regards,
Alejandra Ruiz
Head of ML Ops
Stellarus Robotics
